 JUDGMENT

This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner against the respondents U/s. 22 of Employees Compensation Act, 1923 for seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him, during the course of employment.

The brief facts of the case are as under;
2.
That the petitioner was workman, employed by the first respondent as a 'driver' of the Mahindra Marazzo car bearing registration No.KA-53-AA-0967 and was holding valid and effective driving licence.

On 25.3.2021 at about 23.50 hours as per the directions of the respondent No.1, the petitioner during the course of his employment was driving the car bearing registration No.KA-53-AA-0967 proceeding from Mulbagal town towards NH-75 road, when the petitioner's car reached near Madras NH-75 bypass road, Mulbagal Town, Kolar District, the said car came in contact to the bus bearing registration No.NL-01-B-1914.
Thereby both the vehicles were extensively damaged, the petitioner and one Santhosh sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

3. It is further stated in the petition that, immediately after accident the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Mulbagal and then shifted to Gaurav Orthopaedic & Surgical Hospital, Kolar,
wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.
Due to the accidental injuries, he could not do his work as he was earlier.
4. Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 30 years, working as a driver under the first respondent, by getting salary of Rs.50,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled.
5. Further it is stated that, the Mulbagal Town Police, Mulbagal have registered the case in crime No.25/2021 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.

The accident was occurred during the course of employment with the respondent No.1 as the respondent No.2 was the insurer of the Mahindra Marazzo car bearing No.KA- 53-AA-0967 as on the date of alleged accident.
The respondent No.3 being the another company of the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, this petition.

sentences.text: In response to the notices, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed written statement.
On the other hand, the respondent No.3 has not appeared before the court remained absent, placed exparte.
7. In written statement, respondent No.1 has contended that this petition is not maintainable u/s 22 of the ECA Act, either in law or on facts.
This respondent has not issued any certificate.
Further contended that, the petitioner is the driver cum owner of the vehicle bearing No.KA-53-AA-0967.
The petitioner is nowhere employee under the respondent No.1 and the respondent No.1 is not paying any salary to the petitioner.
Further stated that, petitioner is the owner and he is giving service to the respondent for that he is getting money to that service.
The respondent No.1 has denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner and manner of the accident and also injuries sustained by the petitioner.
He has stated that the Santhosh is the driver to the petitioner and the petitioner is the owner of the vehicle, the petitioner is no more employee under the respondent No.1.
It is also contention of the respondent No.1 that he is not the owner of the car bearing No.KA-53-AA-0967.
With all these grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.
8. The respondent No.2 has contended in its written statement that, the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.

This respondent has also stated that, policy in respect of car bearing No.KA-53- AA-0967 was infavour of the respondent No.1 and it was valid from 1.2.2021 to 31.1.2022, the liability if any is subject to policy terms and conditions.
Further denied the date, time and place of accident and also denied the manner of accident and also the accident has taken place during the course of employment.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition with costs.

9. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties for final determination of this case, my predecessor in office had framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that there is an employee and employer relationship between him and the 1st respondent?
2) Whether the petitioner proves that during the course of employment he had sustained injuries in the accident that occurred on 25.5.2021 at about 23.50 hours when he was driver under the 1st respondent, in respect of vehicle in car bearing No.KA-53-AA-0967 near Madarasa, NH-75 by pass road, Mulbagal town, Kolar District?
3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for any compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
4) What Order or Award?

Further respondent No.2 has examined its Deputy Manager as RW2 and got marked the documents as Ex.R1 to Ex.R5 for consideration.
After the closure of the evidence of the respondent No.2, matter was set down for arguments.
12. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner and respondents.

13. My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative. Issue No.2: In the Affirmative.

14. As these two issues are inter-linked with each other, in order to avoid the repetition of facts and discussions, they are taken together for common discussion.

15. It is the specific case of the petitioner that, he was working as a driver under the respondent No.1, as such, there is a relationship of employee and employer between him and the respondent No.1.

The accident occurred on 25.3.2021, when he was working as a driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-53-AA-0967, during the course of the employment and sustained grievous injuries in the said accident,
16.

On the other hand, it is the strong contention of the respondent No.1 that, there was no employer and employee relationship between him and the petitioner and the alleged accident was not taken place during the course of employment of the petitioner with the respondent No.1.

On the contrary,
the respondent No.2 has not seriously disputed the accident of the petitioner during the course of his employment.
The respondent No.3 remained silent spectator without answering the case of the petitioner.
17. On the basis of all these rival contentions, burden is on the petitioner to prove the above issues by placing, cogent and convincing evidence on record.
18. The petitioner herein, examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P8.
In the affidavit evidence of PW1, reiterated the main petition averments that, as on the date of the accident, he was the driver of car bearing No.KA-53-AA-0967.
During the course of his employment he had sustained injuries, due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the Bus bearing registration No.NL-01-B- 1914.
In this regard, case was registered in crime No.25/2021.

On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one J.Rajan, the S.H.O. of Mulbagal Town Police Station has registered the case against the rider of the car bearing registration No.KA-53-AA-0967 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 338 of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.
22.
At the time of cross-examination of PW1 no material points culled out to disbelieve the relationship of employer and employee between the petitioner and the respondent No.1.
The suggestion put to the witness by the insurance company respondent No.2 to disprove the relationship of employer and employee also been clearly denied by the PW1.
To prove the relationship between the petitioner and the respondent No.1, he has placed identity card marked at Ex.P10.

Except production of identity card, the petitioner has not placed any authenticated documents to show the employee and the employer relationship between him and the respondent No.1.
23.
On the contrary, the respondent No.2- Insurance company has examined the respondent No.1 as RW1.
He has stated in his evidence that, there was no employer and employee relationship between him and the petitioner.
At this stage, the respondent No.1 has turned hostile, the respondent No.2 has cross
-examined the RW1 at length, but nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth.
24. It is the strong assertion of the RW1 that, there was no employer and employee relationship between him and the petitioner.
This witness has been cross-examined by the counsel for the petitioner.
In his cross-examination at para No.1 suggested that, one Santhosh has filed the MVC No.2978/2021 against him, for which he has filed the objection, the said fact has been admitted by the RW1.
The said document marked at Ex.P20 & Ex.P21.

Further suggested that Ex.P22 is the identity card of Santhosh issued by SVT Travells, for which he has admitted that SVT travels also relating to him and he was the partner of the said company.
25.

Apart from this, the counsel for the petitioner has put the question to RW1 about Ex.P5- reply to police notice, in connection with the hiding about the relationship between the respondent No.1 and Nagaraju B.R vs Mvs Transport And Facility Services on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170713435/

26. It is no doubt that, Ex.P5 is the reply to the statement u/s 133 of M.V. act, given by the respondent No.1 to the respondent No.2.
The said assertion has been admitted by the RW1.
Further he has also admitted that bank has seized his vehicle due to non-payment of the installments.

Though he has denied Ex.P10 identity card of the SVT travels, but not placed any document to show that SVT Travels is not belonged to him, moreover, he has admitted in his cross-examination at para No.2 that he is the partner of the SVT Travels.

By considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, it does not create any doubtful situation to disbelieve the assertion of the petitioner about the employer and the employee relationship and also will not give an access to believe the contention of the respondent that, there is no employee and employer relationship between him and the respondent No.1.

If at all, the respondent No.1 is not the owner of the said car bearing No.KA- 53-AA-0967, then question would arises, why he has produced the RC, insurance policy of the car and driving licence of the driver/petitioner before the police to take over his vehicle.
Further, if he has not appointed the petitioner as a driver, why he has mentioned the name of the driver as Nagaraj and his driving licence number as KA5320120004382.
Except denial of the averments of the claim petition, nothing is placed to show that he was not employed the petitioner as driver as on the date of alleged accident.

27. Over all appreciation of aforesaid documents, it is crystal clear that, as on the date of the accident the petitioner was working as a driver in connection with the car bearing No.KA-53-AA-0967 and he was working under the respondent No.1.
Even at the time of cross-examination of RW1 at para No.5 it is clear that, the petitioner was working under him with respect to the vehicle in question.
28. Further, the answers given in connection with the police papers speak about the genuineness of the case of the petitioner.

At the time of the cross- examination of the RW2 also though denied the relationship between the respondent No.1 & the petitioner, but not placed any document on record to disbelieve the relationship between petitioner and the respondent No.1 and the accident occurred during the course of employment.

29. In the light of my discussion held above, the evidence given by the petitioner to the effect that,
on the date of the accident he was the driver of the car bearing No.KA-53-AA-0967 and was driving the same as an employee of the respondent No.1 and the accident occurred during the course of his Nagaraju B.R vs Mvs Transport And Facility Services on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170713435/

sentences.text: Hence, I hold that the petitioner has placed satisfactory evidence to show that there was an employee and the employer relationship between the petitioner and the respondent No.1 and during the course of employment, accident had taken place, consequently, the petitioner has sustained injuries as narrated in the wound certificate marked at Ex.P7.
Hence I am answering the issue No. 1 & 2 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
30.
The petitioner being the injured has approached the court on the ground that, he has sustained grievous injuries during the course of employment.

The petitioner to prove the injuries sustained by him, relied on his affidavit evidence and the documentary evidence as per Ex.P7-wound certificate,
discharge summary as per Ex.P9.

In addition to the evidence of the petitioner, relied on the evidence of the Dr.Imran Hussain, who examined as PW2 and placed clinical examination report, disability form, inpatient record and x-ray pertaining to the petitioner as per Ex.P16 to Ex.P19.
31.
The PW1 in his evidence deposed about the nature of the injuries sustained by him consequent upon the accident.
And placed material document Ex.P7-wound certificate to prove the injuries sustained by him.

As per the wound certificate, the petitioner had sustained the following injuries:
Tenderness and swelling, deformity of right hip Fracture right interochanter of femur 32.
As per the opinion of the doctor, the aforesaid injuries are grievous in nature.
In support of the injuries sustained by the petitioner placed the evidence of Dr. Imran Hussain.
In the evidence of the said witness deposed that, on the history of RTA the petitioner had sustained inter trochanteric fracture of right femur.
In this regard, he was underwent CRIF with IMIL nail for right femur on 27.3.2021.
He was discharged on 30.3.2021.

At the time of his examination, to assess the disability,
noticed that the petitioner has surgical scar mark over right hip, range of motion of right hip flexion-extension normal is 0- 140 degrees, the patient is having reduction of right hip movements.
On the basis of clinical and radiological examination came to the conclusion that, the petitioner is suffering from 45% disability for right lower limb and 15% to the whole body.
In support of his evidence produced clinical examination report, disability assessment form, inpatient record and x-ray as per Ex.P16 to Ex.P19 respectively.
33. At the time of cross-examination of this witness admitted that, now the fractures are united.
Further, denied the suggestion that, the disability will not come in the way of the avocation of the petitioner.
Further, denied the suggestion that, only to help the petitioner he expressed his opinion on a higher side.

34. Over all appreciation o the evidence of PW2 along with the medical documents, it is pertinent to note that, in connection with disability of right lower limb is 45% and whole body disability is 15%.

By looking in to the nature of the injuries, as well as its subsequent effects and also on going through the medical documents, it is apt to take the percentage of the disability to the whole body of the petitioner as 13%, same will meet the ends of justice.

sentences.text: In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, he has placed Aadhar card and driving licence as per Ex.P11 & Ex.P12.
In the said documents, the date of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 13.6.1991.
The alleged accident had taken place on 25.3.2021.
If the said date is taken into consideration as on the date of the accident he was aged about 30 years.
36. In connection with the income of the petitioner, he was working as a driver he used to earn Rs.50,000/- per month.
But no supportive documents placed on record to substantiate the assertion of the petitioner in connection with his salary particulars.
But at the same time, though the respondent No.1 has denied relationship of employer and also with respect to the income of the petitioner.
But, no documentary evidence on record to show the same.
37. As per records, the petitioner was doing driving work.

As such, by considering his work and also the year of the institution of this petition as well as on going through the economic scenario of the year 2021 income of the petitioner is to be taken as per notional income.

In this regard, it is apt to note herein that, In the notification of Ministry of Labour and Employment dated 31.5.2010 which reads like thus;
S.O. 1258(E): In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1B) of Section 4 of the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923 (8 of 1923), the Central Government hereby specifies, for the purposes of Sub-section (1) of the said Section, the following amount as monthly wages, with effect from the date of publication of this Notification in the Official Gazette, viz., "Eight thousand rupees".

Subsequently, the Government of India vide its notification No.S.O.71(E) DATED 3.1.2020 has enhanced the wage ceiling under the Employees' Compensation Act, from Rs.8,000/- to Rs.15,000/-
per month w.e.f. 3.1.2020,
38.
In the case on hand, the accident had occurred on 25.3.2021.

So, by considering the occupation of the petitioner his notional monthly income is taken into consideration as Rs.8.000/- per month,
as the alleged incident had taken place in the year 2021.

39. Apart from this, it is relevant to note that, by virtue of Sec.4 of Employees Compensation Act,
1923, is clear that where the permanent total disablement results from the injury, 60% is to be taken into consideration equal to the monthly wages of the injured multiplied by the relevant factor.

Thus,
the injured notional monthly income is already taken into consideration as Rs.8,000/-.
If 60% is taken into consideration as per Sec.4 of the Employees Compensation 207.98 factor is applicable.

So, the compensation of the petitioner is calculated as follows: Rs.4,800X 207.98 X13/100=
Rs.1,29,779/.

Accordingly, petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,29,779/-.
40.
Added to this, Ex.P13 medical bills reflects that the petitioner has spent Rs.84,771/- towards his treatment due to the accidental injuries during the course of employment.

So, by virtue of S. 4 (2)(A)
Employees Compensation Act 1923 is clear that employee shall be reimbursed actual medical expenditure incurred by him, for treatment of injuries caused during the course of employment.

So,
the petitioner is entitled for Rs.84,771/- towards medical treatment.

sentences.text: In connection with the future treatment, PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner requires surgery for removal of right femur implant costing Rs.35,000/- to Rs.45,000/-.
Relying on the opinion of the doctor it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.25,000/- towards future medication.
42. In the light of the above discussions, I am of the view that, in total the petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,39,550/-.
Therefore Rs.2,39,550/- (Rupees two lakh thirty nine thousand five hundred and fifty only)
is awarded to the petitioner.
LIABILITY 43.

In so far as the liability is concerned, the petitioner has filed this petition against the respondents by showing the respondent No.1 & 3 are the owners of the vehicle and the respondent No.2 is the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
44. On going through the document, Ex.R2- insurance policy in connection with vehicle bearing registration No.KA-53-AA-0967 was valid from 1.2.2021 to 31.1.2022.
The alleged accident had taken place on 25.3.2021.
The said insurance policy was standing in the name of the respondent No.1 as on the date of the accident.
In counter to the said insurance policy, no contra materials are available on record for consideration.
Ex . R3
is the notice issued by the insurance company to the respondent No.1.
Ex. R4
is the postal receipt and the Ex.R5 is the postal acknowledgment.

As such,
the respondent No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

45. Hence, I am of the view that, the respondent No.2, being the insurer of the respondent No.1, is liable to pay the compensation at the rate of 12% p.a. from the date of accident, till its realization,
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.3 as partly affirmative.

ISSUE NO. 4:
46.

In view of my finding on issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 22 of Employees Compensation Act,
1923 is partly allowed, with costs.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation Rs.2,39,550/- (Rupees two lakh thirty nine thousand five hundred and fifty only) together with interest at the rate of 12%
p.a. from the date of accident till its realization.
The respondent No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation amount with interest at the rate of 12% p.a. from the date of accident till its realisation within two months from the date of this order.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner against the respondents U/s. 22 of Employees Compensation Act, 1923 for seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him, during the course of employment.
That the petitioner was workman, employed by the first respondent as a 'driver' of the Mahindra Marazzo car bearing registration No.KA-53-AA-0967 and was holding valid and effective driving licence.
Thereby both the vehicles were extensively damaged, the petitioner and one Santhosh sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Due to the accidental injuries, he could not do his work as he was earlier.
Due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled.
The accident was occurred during the course of employment with the respondent No.1 as the respondent No.2 was the insurer of the Mahindra Marazzo car bearing No.KA- 53-AA-0967 as on the date of alleged accident.
The respondent No.3 being the another company of the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, this petition.

opennyai_summary.issue:
9. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties for final determination of this case, my predecessor in office had framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that there is an employee and employer relationship between him and the 1st respondent?
2) Whether the petitioner proves that during the course of employment he had sustained injuries in the accident that occurred on 25.5.2021 at about 23.50 hours when he was driver under the 1st respondent, in respect of vehicle in car bearing No.KA-53-AA-0967 near Madarasa, NH-75 by pass road, Mulbagal town, Kolar District?
3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for any compensation?
If so, to what extent and from whom?
4) What Order or Award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The accident occurred on 25.3.2021, when he was working as a driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-53-AA-0967, during the course of the employment and sustained grievous injuries in the said accident,
16.
The respondent No.3 remained silent spectator without answering the case of the petitioner.
During the course of his employment he had sustained injuries, due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the Bus bearing registration No.NL-01-B- 1914.
In this regard, case was registered in crime No.25/2021.
Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.
22.
Apart from this, the counsel for the petitioner has put the question to RW1 about Ex.P5- reply to police notice, in connection with the hiding about the relationship between the respondent No.1 and Nagaraju B.R vs Mvs Transport And Facility Services on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170713435/
Though he has denied Ex.P10 identity card of the SVT travels, but not placed any document to show that SVT Travels is not belonged to him, moreover, he has admitted in his cross-examination at para No.2 that he is the partner of the SVT Travels.
By considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, it does not create any doubtful situation to disbelieve the assertion of the petitioner about the employer and the employee relationship and also will not give an access to believe the contention of the respondent that, there is no employee and employer relationship between him and the respondent No.1.
Further, if he has not appointed the petitioner as a driver, why he has mentioned the name of the driver as Nagaraj and his driving licence number as KA5320120004382.
Except denial of the averments of the claim petition, nothing is placed to show that he was not employed the petitioner as driver as on the date of alleged accident.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner has placed satisfactory evidence to show that there was an employee and the employer relationship between the petitioner and the respondent No.1 and during the course of employment, accident had taken place, consequently, the petitioner has sustained injuries as narrated in the wound certificate marked at Ex.P7.
By looking in to the nature of the injuries, as well as its subsequent effects and also on going through the medical documents, it is apt to take the percentage of the disability to the whole body of the petitioner as 13%, same will meet the ends of justice.
As such, by considering his work and also the year of the institution of this petition as well as on going through the economic scenario of the year 2021 income of the petitioner is to be taken as per notional income.
Subsequently, the Government of India vide its notification No.S.O.71(E) DATED 3.1.2020 has enhanced the wage ceiling under the Employees' Compensation Act, from Rs.8,000/- to Rs.15,000/-
per month w.e.f. 3.1.2020,
